We often discuss the role of #AI in energy through percentage gains - efficiency improvements, cost reductions, predictive accuracy. But the real impact is structural: AI is enabling new market dynamics that redefine how energy systems are governed and financed.
 
The foundation is the data infrastructure: smart meters, sensors, and digital grids generate continuous insight into how electricity is actually used. This demand-side visibility creates a national load profile that can enable transformative opportunities,
 
Once governments can see real demand and private sector can act on this #data, new dynamics  emerge:
	•	Auctions can be designed around measured needs, defining clearer requirements for renewables, storage, and flexibility
	•	Investors can leverage data to lower risk and improve project bankability
	•	Markets gain credibility as public data limits discretion and reduces risk of corruption
But the same visibility that empowers can also expose vulnerabilities. Without strong governance, data monopolies, surveillance risks, and algorithmic bias could distort markets rather than open them.
 
The #energy transition will not be powered by new technologies alone, but by the intelligence and integrity of the systems that govern them. Discover how in the newest Sustainable Energy Bulletin 👉 https://lnkd.in/eBAMvFDe
